# CLI Reference

This file is generated from the command tree. Edit command help in `cmd/`
and hand-written notes in `docs/cli/notes/`, then run `make docs`.
`pudl help --json` prints the same tree in machine-readable form.

## Output contract

Use `--help` for inline documentation. Under the global `--json` flag, a
command writes exactly one JSON document to stdout; warnings, progress and
other diagnostics go to stderr, and empty lists are written as `[]`. A few
commands without structured output, such as scaffolding, still print text
under `--json`.

Errors exit nonzero. `pudl check` can also report its findings in the exit
status with `--detailed-exitcode`; see [pudl check](#pudl-check).

## Global flags

These flags apply to every command.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--global` | bool |  | Use the personal ~/.pudl workspace explicitly |
| `--json` | bool |  | Output results as JSON for scripting |

## pudl check

Observe and evaluate exactly the named models; one report

```text
pudl check <model>... [flags]
```

```text
Observe and evaluate exactly the named #SystemModel instances.

Each <model> is a registered #SystemModel, resolved by name (its name field or
short definition name) from the project .pudl/schema and explicitly vendored
packages. Register one with "pudl schema add".

A check runs only the models it names, producers first: a model runs after
every named model it lists in depends_on. A model whose named producer does
not succeed is recorded as blocked. Models that were not named never run.

Each model is observe-only: populate -> drift -> checks. A model without a
populate arm is checks-only: it evaluates its checks over what the catalog
already holds (e.g. data brought in with pudl import). A #CommandObserve
populate runs plain commands that print JSON records (gcloud, kubectl,
aws ... --format=json). Nothing is changed.

A check records one report, whether it names one model or several. Read it
again with "pudl report [ID]".

With --detailed-exitcode the exit status reports the result: 0 clean,
2 drift or a failing fail-severity check, 1 error.

Each check's failing matches are compared with the model's comparable
earlier reports: new, persisting, resolved, or unknown when this observation
cannot establish their absence. With --fail-on new, fail-severity check
failures fail the command (or exit 2) only when one of them is new.

Each finding names its resource's owner, derived from the schema's
_pudl.owner declaration; human output groups findings by owner. --owner TEAM
prints only TEAM's findings (a failed check without one is left out); it does
not narrow the recorded report, its counts or the exit status.

Examples:
    pudl check github-chazu
    pudl check network app --detailed-exitcode
    pudl check network --owner payments
    pudl check network --fail-on new --detailed-exitcode
    pudl check git-inventory --from-catalog --catalog-scope snap_...
    pudl check --populate 'command:gcloud compute networks list --format=json'
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--catalog-scope` | string |  | which already-ingested records --from-catalog replays: an observe snapshot ID, or the origin they were ingested under |
| `--check-upstream` | bool |  | warn if any transitive upstream model (depends_on) is drifted/failed |
| `--detailed-exitcode` | bool |  | exit 0 when clean, 2 when drift or a failing fail-severity check was found, 1 on error |
| `--fail-on` | string | `any` | which fail-severity check failures fail the check: any, or new (a failing match no comparable earlier report recorded) |
| `--from-catalog` | bool |  | drift over already-ingested records (inventory; no live observe); requires --catalog-scope |
| `--owner` | string |  | Print only the findings whose resource this owner owns (_pudl.owner); the recorded report is complete |
| `--populate` | string |  | Check an unregistered observer: command:&lt;cmdline&gt; (a command printing JSON records) |
| `--progress-json` | bool |  | Emit phase progress events as JSON lines on stderr (alongside diagnostics) |

**A check observes and reports; it never changes anything.** For each named
model it runs `populate`, compares `desired` with what was observed, evaluates
the checks and records the result. [Governance](governance.md) is the guide to
checks, findings, policies, waivers, changes over time, owners and CI use.
[Observation](observation-scope.md) covers collectors, fan-out and evidence
selection.

**Exactly the named models.** `pudl check a b c` runs `a`, `b` and `c` and
nothing else. A model runs after every named model it lists in `depends_on`;
dependencies that are not named add no ordering and are never run. When a
named producer does not succeed, its dependents are recorded `blocked`;
independent models continue. The report records the order and the edges
(`ordered_members`, `edges`, `plan_digest`).

**One report.** Each invocation records one report: an aggregate `summary`
(execution, conformity, checks, verification, finding counts, evidence), and
one entry per model under `members` with its result, run ID, summary and full
`report`. Under `--json` that report is the only stdout document. Human output
shows each model's findings as it concludes, then the summary. Read it again
with [`pudl report`](#pudl-report).

**Exit status.** Without `--detailed-exitcode`, a check exits 0 when every
model completed, including when it found drift, and nonzero on a failing
fail-severity check or any error. With it: 0 clean, 2 findings, 1 error. See
[run in CI](governance.md#run-in-ci) for the full rules and `--fail-on new`.

**Checks-only models.** A model without `populate` evaluates its checks over
the catalog as it is, after syncing projected facts. It cannot declare
`desired`.

**Catalog replay is not an observation.** `--from-catalog` compares `desired`
with records already in the catalog, selected by `--catalog-scope` (a
snapshot ID or an import origin). It names exactly one model and never
updates the model's status.

**Interrupting.** The first Ctrl-C (SIGINT or SIGTERM) sends SIGTERM to the
running command and gives it 10 seconds, removes temporary workspaces, and
records the current and remaining models `cancelled`. A second Ctrl-C exits
at once with status 130. A populate `timeout` is recorded as `failed`.

**`--check-upstream`** warns when a model this one transitively depends on is
recorded `drifted` or `failed`; see
[cross-model dependencies](cross-model-dependencies.md).

A model that declares a retired field (`converge`, `plugins`, `inputs`,
`bindings`, sealed values) fails to load with an error naming it; see
[retired commands](retired-commands.md).


```text
Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.
```

## pudl config

View and manage PUDL configuration

```text
pudl config [flags]
```

```text
View and manage PUDL configuration settings.

This command allows you to view the current configuration and see where
your PUDL workspace is located.

The configuration includes:
- Schema repository path (where CUE schemas are stored)
- Data directory path (where imported data is stored)
- Configuration file location

Example usage:
    pudl config                  # Show current configuration
    pudl config --path           # Show configuration file path
    pudl config set <key> <value> # Set a configuration value
    pudl config reset            # Reset to default configuration
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--legacy-dependencies` | bool |  | Inventory ignored global schemas and rules for explicit migration |
| `-p`, `--path` | bool |  | Show configuration file path only |
| `--paths` | bool |  | Show all effective definition and storage paths |

Subcommands:

- [pudl config reset](#pudl-config-reset) — Reset configuration to defaults
- [pudl config set](#pudl-config-set) — Set a configuration value

Inside an initialized repository the configuration is `.pudl/config.yaml`;
otherwise it is `~/.pudl/config.yaml`. Repository `schema_path` and `data_path`
are fixed beneath `.pudl/`; path customization remains a global-mode facility.

## pudl config reset

Reset configuration to defaults

```text
pudl config reset
```

```text
Reset the PUDL configuration to default values.

This will restore:
- Schema path beneath the active .pudl workspace
- Data path beneath the active .pudl workspace
- Version to 1.0

Example usage:
    pudl config reset
```

## pudl config set

Set a configuration value

```text
pudl config set <key> <value>
```

```text
Set a configuration value and save it to the configuration file.

Valid configuration keys:
- schema_path: Path to the schema repository directory
- data_path: Path to the data storage directory
- version: Configuration version

Inside a repository workspace, schema_path and data_path are fixed beneath
.pudl/ and cannot be redirected outside the repository-local state boundary.

Example usage:
    pudl config set schema_path ~/my-schemas
    pudl config set data_path /tmp/pudl-data
    pudl config set version 2.0
```

## pudl delete

Delete a data entry from the catalog

```text
pudl delete <id> [flags]
```

```text
Delete a data entry from the PUDL catalog, including its data file and metadata.

The ID parameter should be the proquint identifier of the data entry as shown
in the 'pudl list' command output.

For collections, use --cascade to remove their memberships and delete items
that no other collection references.
Without --cascade, deleting a collection with items will fail.

Examples:
    pudl delete mivof-duhij                    # Delete with confirmation prompt
    pudl delete mivof-duhij --force            # Delete without confirmation
    pudl delete govim-nupab --cascade          # Delete collection and all its items
    pudl delete mivof-duhij --json             # Output result as JSON
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--cascade` | bool |  | Delete collection and all its items |
| `--force` | bool |  | Delete without confirmation prompt |

Collections with items cannot be deleted without `--cascade`, which removes the
collection's memberships and any items left orphaned. Individual items can
always be deleted.

## pudl doctor

Check workspace health and catalog data, and repair the catalog

```text
pudl doctor [flags]
```

```text
Check workspace structure, integrity, schemas, and retained catalog data.
Catalog records are validated against their assigned schemas. Ordinary inferred imports
also receive a fixed-point inference check; explicit producer assignments are never
reclassified. Use --entry ID to inspect one catalog record, or --health-only for workspace checks.
The catalog scan also warns of likely secrets in stored payloads and current facts,
naming the entry or fact, path and kind, never the value.

Doctor also diagnoses catalog conditions that a repair fixes, and names the repair:
  schema-names  schema names not in canonical <package>.#<Definition> form

  policy-leaves entries assigned to a policy schema instead of its type
  inference     inferred entries whose schema inference now selects another schema
  identity      entries missing a resource_id, or namespaced by a leaf schema
  versions      resources with two entries holding the same version (opt-in:
                applied only when --only names it)
  projections   projected facts that no longer match the catalog or facts specs
  policy-results policy results that are stale (evaluated with an older policy
                digest), orphaned, or never evaluated
  data-permissions  data files or directories group or other users can access
  sensitive-scrub   plaintext stored before a schema declared the field in
                _pudl.sensitive_fields (opt-in: applied only when --only names it)

Without --fix nothing is written. --fix applies every repair (or those named by
--only) in that order; --fix --dry-run previews them. The sensitive scrub
re-derives the IDs of the entries it rewrites (old IDs still resolve) and
compacts the catalog; fact history and exported bundles keep the plaintext, so
rotate every credential it redacts.
```

Examples:

```bash
pudl doctor
  pudl doctor --fix --dry-run
  pudl doctor --fix --only projections
  pudl doctor --fix --dry-run --only sensitive-scrub
  pudl doctor --fix --only inference --schema pudl/core.#Item --include-explicit
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | With --fix, report what the repairs would change without writing |
| `--entry` | string |  | Check one catalog entry by proquint or full ID |
| `--fix` | bool |  | Apply the diagnosed repairs |
| `--health-only` | bool |  | Check workspace health without scanning catalog records |
| `--include-explicit` | bool |  | Re-infer every entry in scope, including explicit assignments and invalid entries |
| `--only` | stringSlice |  | Limit repairs to these names: schema-names, policy-leaves, inference, identity, versions, projections, policy-results, data-permissions, sensitive-scrub |
| `--origin` | string |  | Check and repair only entries from this origin |
| `--schema` | string |  | Check and repair only entries assigned to this schema |
| `--verify-payloads` | bool |  | Verify referenced raw payload hashes without repairing evidence |

**Diagnose, then repair.** Plain `doctor` writes nothing. It checks
workspace health (schema packages that fail to load, `base_schema` cycles,
invalid Datalog rules with their file positions), validates catalog records
against their schemas, scans for likely secrets, and lists each repair that is
needed. `--fix` applies the needed repairs in the order listed in `--help` and
re-checks the catalog; `--fix --only NAME` limits them; `--fix --dry-run`
previews them. `--fix` refuses to write when a health check failed. A repair
that changes entries also resyncs projected facts.

**Scope.** `--entry` checks one record and cannot be combined with
`--health-only`. `--schema` and `--origin` scope the catalog scan and the
inference repair. The inference repair reclassifies only inferred entries the
scan found drifted; `--include-explicit` re-infers every entry in scope,
explicit assignments included. The identity repair backfills missing
`resource_id`s and recomputes those an older release namespaced by the leaf
schema.

**`versions`** renumbers each resource whose history holds two entries with
the same version, 1..N in import order. Observation ingest before pudl-42w
recorded every observed entry as version 1, so a resource observed in several
states (a model whose definition changed, say) has several version-1 entries.
It runs only when named: `--fix --only versions`.

**Likely secrets.** The scan reports likely secrets (known token formats and
a conservative entropy check) in stored payloads outside `sensitive_fields`
and `secret_scan_ignore`, and in the args of current facts, skipping facts
projection copied from payloads. Findings name the entry or fact, path and
kind, never the value. They are warnings and do not change `ok` or the exit
status.

**`sensitive-scrub`** removes plaintext stored before a schema declared the
path in `_pudl.sensitive_fields`, from payloads, collection and metadata
files, snapshot files, stored reports and legacy files. It runs only when
named: `--fix --only sensitive-scrub` (with `--dry-run` to preview). It
rewrites each artifact as a fresh import would store it, re-derives the ID of
each changed entry (old IDs and proquints still resolve), re-projects facts,
and compacts SQLite. Non-JSON or compressed payloads are listed as
unsupported: delete and re-import them. Fact history and exported bundles keep
the plaintext, so rotate every credential the scrub redacts.

**JSON.** `report_version` 3 with `mode` (`diagnose`, `dry-run` or `fix`),
`ok`, `health`, `catalog`, `secrets` (absent when the catalog was not
scanned), `repairs` and any setup `error`. Each repair has `name`,
`condition`, `status` (`ok`, `needed`, `applied`, `partial`, `error` or
`skipped`), `message`, `pending`, `changed`, `failed`, `changes`, `errors`,
optional `details`, and, when needed, `preview_argv` and `apply_argv`.
Invalid records, inference mismatches, failed health checks, and an `error`
or `partial` repair exit nonzero. An empty catalog is valid.

`--verify-payloads` checks referenced files and their SHA256 content claims.
It never repairs evidence.

## pudl example

Install bundled examples into this workspace

Subcommands:

## pudl example install

Install a runnable example and its fixture data

```text
pudl example install <name> [flags]
```

```text
Install a bundled example in the current initialized PUDL workspace,
or with --global in the personal ~/.pudl workspace (after pudl init --global).
No source checkout or download is needed.

Installing again upgrades the example: files you have not edited since pudl
installed them are replaced with this version's, and new files are added.
Files you edited, and files from an install by an older pudl (which kept no
record of what it wrote), are conflicts: nothing is written and each is
listed. --overwrite replaces them, keeping your versions as <file>.bak.

The git-inventory example includes a model expecting default branch main and
baseline and changed inventories. The model observes the current inventory
with cat, so the tutorial needs nothing beyond PUDL.

The gcp-network-hygiene example includes a firewall type and policy, a
fixture observer, a check over policy results, a corrected fixture, and a
separate gcloud-based live model.

The gcp content pack includes draft schemas for the core GCP inventory,
best-practice policies, gcloud and fixture collectors, and three check
families: network hygiene, data protection and GKE posture.

The aws content pack does the same for AWS, with aws CLI and fixture
collectors and three check families: network exposure, data protection and
identity posture.

Example:
    pudl init
    pudl example install git-inventory
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--overwrite` | bool |  | Replace files that differ from this version, keeping yours as &lt;file&gt;.bak |

Available examples: `git-inventory`, `gcp-network-hygiene`, `gcp` and `aws`.
Each includes its model and fixture data; no checkout or download is needed.
Identical files are left alone. Conflicting edits or symlinked destinations
cause an error before installation writes files. This command does not
initialize global state.

`gcp` is a content pack: draft schemas for the core GCP inventory,
best-practice policies, gcloud and fixture collectors, and three check
families. See [the pack README](../examples/gcp/README.md).

`aws` is the AWS content pack: draft schemas for VPC networking, EC2, EBS,
S3, RDS, KMS and IAM, best-practice policies, relationship and impact rules,
aws CLI and fixture collectors, and three check families. See
[the pack README](../examples/aws/README.md).

`--json` returns `example`, the workspace `root`, and relative `files` paths.
See [getting started](getting-started.md) for the Git inventory tutorial; it
needs only PUDL, Git, `cat` and `cp`.

## pudl export

Export data lake entries to various formats

```text
pudl export [flags]
```

```text
Export data from the PUDL catalog to various formats.

You can export entries by ID, schema, or origin. The data is exported in the
specified format (JSON, YAML, CSV, or NDJSON).

Examples:
    pudl export --id babod-fakak                  # Export single entry by proquint ID
    pudl export --schema aws.#EC2Instance         # Export all EC2 instances
    pudl export --origin k8s-pods --format yaml   # Export K8s pods as YAML
    pudl export --id babod-fakak --output out.json  # Export to file
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--allow-partial` | bool |  | Publish readable entries on input errors; report incomplete output with a nonzero exit |
| `--bundle` | string |  | Write a verified portable workspace bundle |
| `--format` | string | `json` | Output format: json, yaml, csv, ndjson |
| `--id` | string |  | Export entry by proquint ID |
| `--max-bundle-bytes` | int64 | `17179869184` | Maximum uncompressed bundle bytes |
| `--origin` | string |  | Export entries from origin |
| `-o`, `--output` | string |  | Output file (default: stdout) |
| `--pretty` | bool | `true` | Pretty-print output |
| `--schema` | string |  | Export entries matching schema |

Exports honor source formats and collection membership. Read/serialization failures
fail by default; `--allow-partial` publishes readable entries with a nonzero exit
and explicit diagnostics. File destinations are replaced atomically after success.
CSV columns are sorted and support scalar object fields.

`--bundle FILE` captures the complete local workspace, without entry filters.
See [evidence and recovery](evidence.md) for portable bundles, limits, and restore.

To print one entry's payload exactly as stored — no header, numbers intact —
for piping into other tools, export it: `pudl export --id <proquint> --format json`.
For a collection this yields its items' records.

## pudl facts

Query the bitemporal fact store

```text
pudl facts
```

```text
Inspect facts stored in the bitemporal fact store. Everyday queries go
through 'pudl query'; these subcommands look at stored facts directly.

Available subcommands:
- list:       Query facts by relation with temporal filtering
- show:       Inspect a single fact by ID
- search:     Full-text search over currently-valid facts
- stats:      Aggregate statistics over the fact store

Writing facts and changing their lifecycle (add, retract, invalidate) are
advanced commands, left out of this list; see 'pudl guide query'.

Examples:
    pudl facts list --relation observation
    pudl facts show abc123...
    pudl facts search "timeout" --relation config
```

Subcommands:

- [pudl facts list](#pudl-facts-list) — List facts from the bitemporal store
- [pudl facts search](#pudl-facts-search) — Full-text search over currently-valid facts
- [pudl facts show](#pudl-facts-show) — Show details of a single fact
- [pudl facts stats](#pudl-facts-stats) — Aggregate statistics over the fact store

Advanced subcommands:

- [pudl facts add](#pudl-facts-add) — Add a fact to the bitemporal store (the canonical write)
- [pudl facts invalidate](#pudl-facts-invalidate) — Invalidate a fact (mark as no longer true)
- [pudl facts retract](#pudl-facts-retract) — Retract a fact (mark as no longer asserted)

## pudl facts list

List facts from the bitemporal store

```text
pudl facts list [flags]
```

```text
Query facts by relation with optional temporal and source filtering.

Temporal modes (determined by which flags are set):
  (none)           Current facts: valid now, not retracted
  --as-of-valid    What was true at a point in time (current knowledge)
  --as-of-tx       What we believed at a point in time
  (both)           What we believed at --as-of-tx about what was true at --as-of-valid
  --as-of-tx-seq   What we believed right after write sequence N (exact; use
                   instead of --as-of-tx to separate writes in the same second)

Time format: RFC3339 (e.g. 2026-04-01T14:30:00Z) or Unix timestamp.
--as-of-tx means the state after every write during or before that second, so
a fact recorded and retracted within one second appears only by sequence.

Examples:
    pudl facts list --relation observation
    pudl facts list --relation observation --source claude-code
    pudl facts list --relation depends --as-of-valid 2026-04-01T14:30:00Z
    pudl facts list --relation observation --json
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--as-of-tx` | string |  | Query transaction time (RFC3339 or Unix timestamp) |
| `--as-of-tx-seq` | int64 |  | Query by write sequence instead of --as-of-tx (exact within one second) |
| `--as-of-valid` | string |  | Query valid time (RFC3339 or Unix timestamp) |
| `--relation` | string |  | Relation to query (required) |
| `--source` | string |  | Filter by source |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | bool |  | Show full fact details |

`--as-of-valid` asks what was true at a moment; `--as-of-tx` asks what the store
believed at a moment, in whole seconds, after every write during or before that
second. `--as-of-tx-seq` selects an exact write in the store's transaction
sequence, which also shows facts added and retracted within one second. See
[facts](facts.md) for the bitemporal model.

## pudl facts search

Full-text search over currently-valid facts

```text
pudl facts search <query> [flags]
```

```text
Keyword search over the indexed text of currently-valid facts, best matches
first. The index covers the values of each fact's args (not the JSON keys).

The query uses SQLite FTS5 syntax: bare terms are ANDed, "quoted phrases" match
in order, a trailing * is a prefix match, and AND/OR/NOT combine terms. A term
with punctuation, such as prod-nat or 10.0.0.1, is matched as a phrase.

Examples:
    pudl facts search "rate limiting"
    pudl facts search "circular dependency" --relation observation
    pudl facts search "auth*" --limit 10
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--limit` | int | `20` | Maximum results (0 = no limit) |
| `--relation` | string |  | Limit search to a relation |

Search uses SQLite FTS5 query syntax over the values of currently valid facts,
best matches first. A term with punctuation, such as `prod-nat` or
`10.0.0.1`, is matched as a phrase.

## pudl facts show

Show details of a single fact

```text
pudl facts show <id> [flags]
```

```text
Display full details of a fact by its ID.

Accepts the full 64-character hex ID or a unique prefix.

Invalidation records a new version of a fact rather than rewriting the old
one. An ID of a superseded version shows the fact's newest version; pass
--exact to show the version the ID names as it was recorded.

Examples:
    pudl facts show c0b4392d347aca8e517c9bb8775a78951c6214e07f04f9168dbe3fbfa862e32a
    pudl facts show c0b4392d347a
    pudl facts show c0b4392d347a --exact
    pudl facts show c0b4392d347a --json
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--exact` | bool |  | Show the version this ID names instead of the newest version |

## pudl facts stats

Aggregate statistics over the fact store

```text
pudl facts stats [flags]
```

```text
Show counts grouped by relation, kind, scope, source, or any arg field.

Without --group-by, shows count per relation, including when --relation filters
the data. Explicit --group-by selects source or an arbitrary args field.

Supports comma-separated field names for cross-tabulation.

Examples:
    pudl facts stats
    pudl facts stats --relation observation
    pudl facts stats --relation observation --group-by kind
    pudl facts stats --group-by scope
    pudl facts stats --group-by kind,scope
    pudl facts stats --relation observation --group-by source
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--group-by` | string |  | Comma-separated fields to group by (e.g. kind,scope) |
| `--relation` | string |  | Filter to specific relation |

Without `--group-by`, counts are grouped by `relation`, including when a
relation filter is supplied. Explicit grouping can select `source` or any args
field; several comma-separated fields produce a cross-tabulation.

## pudl graph

Export the resource graph

```text
pudl graph
```

```text
Work with the resource graph: cataloged resources and the relationships
between them, as read by the web graph explorer (web/).

Available subcommands:
- export:  Write the current resource graph as JSON
- vocab:   Show what pudl ui knows about resource and relationship types
```

Subcommands:

- [pudl graph export](#pudl-graph-export) — Write the current resource graph as JSON
- [pudl graph vocab](#pudl-graph-vocab) — Show what pudl ui knows about resource and relationship types

## pudl graph export

Write the current resource graph as JSON

```text
pudl graph export [flags]
```

```text
Write the current resource graph as JSON, in the canonical graph format the
web explorer loads (docs/frontend.md#backend-integration).

Resources are the catalog's current entries, one per resource. Each schema's
optional _pudl.graph block names the fields used for name, account, region and
zone, and the values other records use to refer to the resource.

Relationships come from Datalog rules whose head is the reserved relation

    graph_edge(type, source, target, basis)

where source and target are a resource ID or a reference value such as an
AWS ID or a GCP path. A reference that matches no cataloged resource is kept
as "ref:<value>", so the graph shows the resource as unknown instead of
dropping the edge. Problems (unreadable payloads, ambiguous references, rules
that fail) are listed in meta.warnings and never stop the export.

The vocabulary field carries everything the explorer knows about types and
relationship types, read from CUE: display info and view roles from each
schema's _pudl.graph block, and graph_edge_type, graph_edge_category,
graph_provider, graph_account_type and graph_resource_type facts from rule
files. 'pudl graph vocab' shows it.

--as-of exports the graph as pudl had recorded it at a past time: each
resource's latest entry by then, the snapshots taken by then, and facts as
believed then about then. Rules and schemas are always today's, and entries
deleted since cannot be shown.

Output is always JSON; the global --json flag changes nothing.

Examples:
    pudl graph export > graph.json
    pudl graph export -o web/public/graph.json
    pudl graph export --as-of 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--as-of` | string |  | Export the graph as recorded at this time (RFC3339 or Unix seconds) |
| `-o`, `--output` | string |  | Output file (default: stdout) |

## pudl graph vocab

Show what pudl ui knows about resource and relationship types

```text
pudl graph vocab
```

```text
Show the graph vocabulary: everything pudl ui knows about types, read from
CUE. pudl ui has no type knowledge of its own; a type or relationship missing
here is drawn as unknown.

- Resource types: each schema's _pudl graph block (display {code, label,
  class} and view roles), plus graph_resource_type facts for types with no
  schema.
- Edge types and categories: graph_edge_type and graph_edge_category facts
  in rule files (pudl/rules/*.cue).
- Providers: graph_provider facts; graph_account_type names the type a
  provider's account attribute refers to.

Problems lists what will not draw as intended: cataloged types with no display
info, graph_edge rules deriving undeclared types, roles naming undeclared edge
types, unknown categories and conflicting declarations. pudl doctor reports
the same problems.

--json prints exactly the vocabulary field of pudl graph export.

See docs/schema-authoring.md, "Make a type appear in pudl ui".
```

Examples:

```bash
pudl graph vocab
  pudl graph vocab --json | jq '.problems'
```

## pudl guide

Quick-reference guide for agents and humans

```text
pudl guide [topic]
```

```text
Print usage guides for pudl features and concepts.

Run 'pudl guide' with no arguments to see all available topics.
Run 'pudl guide <topic>' to read a specific guide.
```

## pudl import

Import data into PUDL data lake

```text
pudl import [paths...] [--path <file|dir|pattern>] [flags]
```

```text
Import data from files into the PUDL data lake with automatic format detection
and schema assignment.

This command imports data from various formats (JSON, YAML, CSV, NDJSON) and stores it
in the PUDL data lake with full metadata tracking. Raw and metadata files use
content-addressed names.

Paths may be given as arguments, with --path, or both. Each accepts a single
file, a wildcard pattern, or a directory (an unquoted pattern the shell has
already expanded arrives as several arguments and is imported in full):
- Single file: --path data.json
- Wildcard patterns: --path *.json, --path data/*.yaml, --path logs/2024-*.json
- Directory: --path exports/ imports its .json/.ndjson/.jsonl/.yaml/.yml/.csv
  files (compressed .gz/.zst variants included); add --recursive to descend
  into subdirectories. Hidden files and directories are skipped.

With --json, the command prints one JSON array with an entry per file:
the import result fields plus "status" (imported, skipped, or failed) and,
for a failure, "error". Progress lines go to stderr.

Data Storage:
- In a repository workspace: .pudl/data/{raw,metadata,sqlite}/
- Outside one: ~/.pudl/data/{raw,metadata,sqlite}/
- The repository and global catalogs are separate; imports never cross them

Schema Assignment:
- Explicit schema validation with --schema (strict unless --allow-schema-fallback)
- Automatic schema inference from CUE schemas in the schema repository
- Chained validation: type → base type → catchall; --schema must name a type, never a policy
- Untyped imports use best-effort inference; explicit schemas must validate


Compressed Input:
- .gz and .zst files (or gzip/zstd magic bytes) are decompressed before import;
  the decompressed bytes are what is hashed, stored, and parsed

Reading from stdin:
- Pipe data with no --path, or use --path - ; set --format when content
  detection is ambiguous

Example usage:
    # Single file import
    pudl import --path data.json
    pudl import --path aws-instances.json --schema aws.ec2
    pudl import --path k8s-pods.yaml --schema k8s.pod --origin k8s-get-pods


    # Several files, or a shell-expanded glob
    pudl import fw-prod-a.json fw-prod-b.json
    pudl import exports/*.json

    # Wildcard batch import
    pudl import --path '*.json'
    pudl import --path data/*.yaml
    pudl import --path logs/2024-01-*.json

    # Check classification, identity and redaction first; nothing is written
    pudl import fw-prod-a.json --schema 'pudl/gcp.#Firewall' --dry-run

    # Add a field gcloud omits, on every record
    pudl import fw-prod-a.json --schema 'pudl/gcp.#Firewall' --set project=prod-a

    # From stdin
    cat data.json | pudl import
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--allow-schema-fallback` | bool |  | Explicitly allow records that do not satisfy --schema (reports fallback) |
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | Show how records would be classified, identified, redacted and projected; write nothing |
| `--explain` | bool |  | Explain original schema candidates, fallback, and search-path shadowing |
| `--format` | string |  | Specify format for stdin data (json, yaml, csv, ndjson) |
| `--max-decoded-bytes` | int64 | `1073741824` | Maximum decoded source bytes per file |
| `--max-record-bytes` | int64 | `67108864` | Maximum decoded JSON record size |
| `--max-staging-bytes` | int64 | `2147483648` | Maximum prepared source and record bytes per file |
| `--origin` | string |  | Override origin detection (optional) |
| `-p`, `--path` | string |  | Path to file or wildcard pattern to import (use '-' for stdin) |
| `--recursive` | bool |  | When --path is a directory, also import supported files in its subdirectories |
| `--schema` | string |  | Specify schema for validation (e.g., aws.ec2) |
| `--set` | stringArray |  | Set a field on every record: path=value (repeatable; overwrites; JSON values keep their type, '"…"' forces a string) |

Behavior:

- Duplicate files (same content hash) are skipped automatically.
- Without `--path`, data is read from piped stdin; `--format` names its format.
- A directory imports its supported files; `--recursive` descends into
  subdirectories. Hidden entries are skipped.
- NDJSON files and top-level JSON arrays are split into collections with
  individual items. Numbers are kept exactly as written.
- CSV rows keep every cell verbatim as text (`"00123"` stays `"00123"`).
- `.gz` and `.zst` files are decompressed; the stored data, hash, size and
  inference all use the decompressed content.
- `--schema` requires every record to satisfy that schema. Unavailable schemas
  and mismatches fail, including on dedup re-import and `--dry-run`.
- `--allow-schema-fallback` explicitly permits base/catchall fallback. JSON
  reports `requested_schema`, `schema_policy`, and `schema_mismatches`.
- The atomic unit is one input file (all collection records together). In a
  multi-file import, successful files remain committed and failures are reported
  per file with a nonzero command exit. A command observation is one atomic batch
  across all its runs; invalid records prevent publication of that batch.
- Format is detected from extension and content; origin from the filename.

Set `PUDL_DEBUG=1` for detailed error output.

`--explain` exposes classification/fallback reasons and schema sources. Byte limits bound records, decoded input, and staging; failures never truncate records. See [evidence](evidence.md).

Paths can be given as arguments too (`pudl import a.json exports/*.json`), so a
shell-expanded glob imports every file. Named paths win over piped stdin.

`--set path=value` (repeatable) writes a field into every record before
anything else happens — e.g. the `project` gcloud leaves out. It overwrites;
values are typed like JSON (`'"123"'` forces a string). JSON/NDJSON only.

`--dry-run` classifies, identifies, redacts and projects every record and
writes nothing: per-schema counts, records already cataloged (and how many a
`--schema` would move), validation failures with their first issues,
unresolved identity, projected facts and records that matched more than one
schema family.

Re-importing data that is already cataloged with a `--schema` it satisfies
moves those entries to that schema. A re-import is also an observation: the
records' projected facts become current again.

Records of schemas declaring `sensitive_fields` are redacted before storage;
schemas declaring `facts` project into the fact store. Likely secrets outside
the sensitive fields are reported by record, path and kind (never the value)
and are not rewritten. See [projection](projection.md).

## pudl init

Initialize or repair a local PUDL workspace (--global for ~/.pudl)

```text
pudl init [flags]
```

```text
Create a self-contained .pudl/ in the current directory, including
configuration, schemas, local data directories, and bundled agent skills.
Repeating initialization repairs owned files while preserving authored configuration.
Use --force to replace configuration, or --global to initialize ~/.pudl instead.
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--force` | bool |  | Replace authored workspace configuration |
| `--from-bundle` | string |  | Restore verified history into a new local workspace; legacy pending approvals are rejected |
| `--max-bundle-bytes` | int64 | `17179869184` | Maximum uncompressed restored bundle bytes |

Initialization installs configuration, a local CUE module and built-in schemas,
authoring and data directories, and bundled Claude skills. Repeated
initialization preserves authored configuration; `--force` replaces
configuration while preserving data.

`--json` returns the workspace `path` and `mode`.

`--from-bundle FILE` restores a verified bundle into a new workspace and never
overwrites existing state. Restored snapshots do not count as a model's latest
observation until the model is observed again. See
[backup and restore](evidence.md#backup-and-restore).

## pudl list

List imported data in the PUDL data lake

```text
pudl list [flags]
```

```text
List and query imported data in the PUDL data lake with filtering and sorting options.

This command displays imported data from the active catalog, including metadata
such as schema assignments, timestamps, sizes, and record counts. In a repository
workspace all records in its local catalog are visible unless --origin is supplied.

Filtering Options:
- --schema: Filter by CUE schema (e.g., aws.#EC2Instance, k8s.#Pod)
- --origin: Filter by data origin (e.g., aws-ec2, k8s-pods)
- --format: Filter by file format (json, yaml, csv, ndjson)
- --collection-id: Filter by collection ID (show items from specific collection)
- --collections-only: Show only collection entries (not individual items)
- --items-only: Show only individual items (not collections)
- --item-id: Filter by specific item ID

Display Options:
- --verbose: Show detailed information including file paths
- --limit: Cap the total number of results across all pages (default: no cap)
- --sort-by: Sort by field (timestamp, size, records, schema, origin)
- --reverse: Reverse sort order
- --fancy: Use interactive bubbletea interface with filtering (press / to filter, enter to show details with raw data)

Examples:
    pudl list                                    # List the active catalog
    pudl list --schema aws.#EC2Instance          # List only EC2 instances
    pudl list --origin k8s-pods                  # List Kubernetes pod data
    pudl list --format ndjson --verbose         # List NDJSON collections with details
    pudl list --collections-only                # Show only collections
    pudl list --items-only                      # Show only individual items
    pudl list --collection-id my-collection     # Show items from specific collection
    pudl list --sort-by size --reverse          # List by size, largest first
    pudl list --limit 10                        # Show only first 10 entries
    pudl list --fancy                           # Interactive list with filtering and detailed view
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--all` | bool |  | Return all matching entries in one result (still respects --limit) |
| `--artifacts` | bool |  | Show only legacy run artifacts (mu manifests and manifest actions) |
| `--collection-id` | string |  | Filter by collection ID |
| `--collections-only` | bool |  | Show only collections |
| `--fancy` | bool |  | Use interactive bubbletea interface with filtering |
| `--format` | string |  | Filter by file format (json, yaml, csv, ndjson) |
| `--item-id` | string |  | Filter by item ID |
| `--items-only` | bool |  | Show only individual items |
| `--limit` | int |  | Cap the total number of results across all pages (0 = no cap) |
| `--origin` | string |  | Filter by data origin (e.g., aws-ec2) |
| `--page` | int | `1` | Page number (1-based) |
| `--per-page` | int | `20` | Results per page |
| `--reverse` | bool |  | Reverse sort order |
| `--schema` | string |  | Filter by CUE schema: a value with # matches whole definition names (aws.#EC2Instance, #Route); otherwise a substring |
| `--select` | stringArray |  | Include this payload field in results (repeatable) |
| `--sort-by` | string | `timestamp` | Sort by field (timestamp, size, records, schema, origin) |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | bool |  | Show detailed information |
| `--where` | stringArray |  | Filter payloads by path=value; repeat for AND, wildcards match any element |

`--schema` with a `#` matches whole definition names: `pudl/gcp.#Route`,
`gcp.#Route` and `#Route` all find routes but not `#Router`. A value without
`#` (`gcp`, `Route`) is a substring match. `--origin` and `--format` are
substring matches; `%` and `_` match literally.

`--json` prints one object, not an array, and it is **paginated** (`--per-page`
defaults to 20):

```json
{
  "entries": [{"id": "…", "proquint": "…", "schema": "…", "origin": "…",
               "format": "…", "size_bytes": 0, "record_count": 0,
               "import_timestamp": "…", "stored_path": "…", "metadata_path": "…",
               "confidence": 1, "collection_type": "item", "collection_id": "…",
               "item_id": "…", "item_index": 0}],
  "total_entries": 0, "total_matched": 0, "total_pages": 0, "current_page": 1,
  "summary": {"total_size_bytes": 0, "total_records": 0, "unique_schemas": 0,
              "unique_origins": 0, "unique_formats": 0}
}
```

Count matches with `total_matched` (not `entries | length`). `summary` sizes
and record totals cover the current page; its `unique_*` counts cover the whole
catalog; it is omitted when nothing matches.

`--all` returns every match in one result and still respects `--limit`. It cannot
be combined with `--page`. `--where path=value` filters decoded payloads using
typed equality; wildcards match any element, and repeated conditions are ANDed.
`--select path` includes chosen fields (repeatable). These operations inspect
individual records, skipping collection containers. Filtering precedes pagination.
Unreadable payloads fail the command. Inspection has a 64 MiB per-record and
256 MiB total scan budget; narrow schema or collection scope for larger data.
`--fancy` remains available and can display the filtered record set.

## pudl model

Manage #SystemModel definitions

```text
pudl model
```

```text
Manage registered #SystemModel definitions.

A #SystemModel is registered as a CUE definition inheriting #SystemModel in the
schema repository (project .pudl/schema or global ~/.pudl/schema).
```

Subcommands:

- [pudl model deps](#pudl-model-deps) — Refresh and show the cross-model dependency graph
- [pudl model list](#pudl-model-list) — List registered #SystemModel definitions
- [pudl model new](#pudl-model-new) — Scaffold a #SystemModel observer
- [pudl model show](#pudl-model-show) — Show a registered #SystemModel definition
- [pudl model validate](#pudl-model-validate) — Validate a registered #SystemModel without running it

A model is a registered `#SystemModel` in `.pudl/schema/models/`: a
`populate` collector, its `observation` scope, optional `desired` state,
`checks`, `waivers` and `depends_on`. A model without `populate` is
checks-only. `pudl check MODEL...` runs models; nothing here changes
infrastructure. See [observation](observation-scope.md) for collectors and
[governance](governance.md) for checks and waivers.

## pudl model deps

Refresh and show the cross-model dependency graph

```text
pudl model deps
```

```text
Reconcile every registered model's declared depends_on edges into model_depends_on
facts WITHOUT running the models, then print the dependency graph.

This closes the run-time-only coverage gap: querying impact (impacted_by) is
otherwise blind to models that have never been run. 'pudl model deps' records
every declared edge from the schema directly.

Examples:
    pudl model deps
    pudl model deps --json
```

`deps` records each registered model's declared `depends_on` as
`model_depends_on` facts without running any model, so impact queries
(`pudl query impacted_by changed=MODEL`) cover models that were never
checked. Edges recorded by retired features are labeled by their source,
such as `binding`. See [dependencies and impact](cross-model-dependencies.md).

## pudl model list

List registered #SystemModel definitions

```text
pudl model list
```

```text
List every #SystemModel-derived definition registered in the schema
repository (project definitions precede explicitly vendored packages), with its
populate kind and desired/check counts.

This is the static registry of runnable models — what 'pudl check <name>' can
resolve — independent of whether a model has been checked yet.
```

## pudl model new

Scaffold a #SystemModel observer

```text
pudl model new <name> [flags]
```

```text
Create a registered #SystemModel scaffold in the project schema (or the
global schema outside a workspace). The scaffold observes with #CommandObserve:
commands that print JSON records, run directly by pudl (no shell). Always edit
the returned file to add desired state or checks.

--populate command:<cmdline> sets the command. Without it the scaffold runs a
placeholder command that prints no records; replace it before relying on it.

Examples:
    pudl model new gcp-firewalls --populate 'command:gcloud compute firewall-rules list --format=json'
    pudl model new inventory
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--check` | string |  | Save an existing query relation as a checks-only model |
| `--evidence` | stringArray |  | Saved check evidence selector (snapshot ID, model:name or scope:name; repeatable) |
| `--expect` | string | `empty` | Saved check expectation: empty or nonempty |
| `--force` | bool |  | Replace an existing scaffold file |
| `--max-age` | string |  | Maximum age for the saved check's selected observations |
| `--populate` | string |  | Populate command: command:&lt;cmdline&gt; (default: a placeholder printing no records) |

## pudl model show

Show a registered #SystemModel definition

```text
pudl model show <name>
```

```text
Show the details of a registered #SystemModel by name (the instance's
'name:' field or its short definition name): populate arm, desired state,
and checks.
```

Human output resolves desired resource-type tags to retrievable schema names;
JSON retains the model's original routing tags.

## pudl model validate

Validate a registered #SystemModel without running it

```text
pudl model validate <name>
```

```text
Resolve and validate a #SystemModel by name. It validates the authored
CUE template and runs structural checks on its arms without touching any external
system.
```

A model is validated as authored: CUE decode, structural checks on its arms,
and its schema contracts. A model that still declares a retired field (such as
`inputs` or `bindings`) fails with an error naming the field.

## pudl policy

Evaluate compliance policies against cataloged resources

```text
pudl policy
```

```text
Compliance policies are schemas with _pudl.schema_type: "policy" that name
their type through _pudl.base_schema. Every import and observation evaluates the
applicable policies per resource and stores the results as facts:

  policy_status(resource, policy, type, status, policy_digest)
  policy_violation(resource, policy, rule, severity, path, kind, declared_by)

Status is compliant, noncompliant or unknown (a constrained field was absent).
The built-in rule policy_noncompliant(resource, policy, severity) serves checks.
A result is stale when its digest differs from the loaded policy's; pudl doctor
reports stale results and pudl policy evaluate refreshes them.
```

Subcommands:

- [pudl policy evaluate](#pudl-policy-evaluate) — Re-evaluate policies against stored current resources
- [pudl policy list](#pudl-policy-list) — List loaded policies with their stored result counts
- [pudl policy show](#pudl-policy-show) — Show a policy's rules, inheritance and failing resources

Policies are written in CUE ([Compliance Policies](schema-authoring.md#compliance-policies)).
pudl evaluates them after every import and observation; these commands
inspect the stored results and re-evaluate them. Results are facts
(`policy_status`, `policy_violation`), so `pudl query` and checks read them;
the built-in rule `policy_noncompliant` is the usual check query (see
[governance](governance.md#use-policies-in-checks)). A result is stale when
the policy or its type changed since it was evaluated; `pudl policy evaluate`
or `pudl doctor --fix --only policy-results` refreshes it.

## pudl policy evaluate

Re-evaluate policies against stored current resources

```text
pudl policy evaluate [POLICY...] [flags]
```

```text
Re-evaluate compliance policies against every stored current resource, from
its retained payload, without re-importing. Changed results replace the current
policy_status and policy_violation facts; history keeps the previous result and
the policy digest it was evaluated with. Results of policies that no longer apply,
or are no longer loaded, are closed. A policy that fails to load is reported and
its results are left unchanged.

Name policies to evaluate only those. --dry-run reports what would change and
writes nothing.

--what-if FILE evaluates a draft policy file that is not installed: it is loaded
beside the installed schemas (shadowing an installed policy of the same name),
evaluated against the stored current resources, and reported as status counts and
the top violations. Nothing is written. The draft must be standalone CUE (its
policies name their type through _pudl.base_schema).
```

Examples:

```bash
pudl policy evaluate
  pudl policy evaluate pudl/aws.#S3BucketBestPractice --dry-run
  pudl policy evaluate --what-if drafts/s3_strict.cue --json
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | Report what would change without writing |
| `--what-if` | string |  | Evaluate a draft policy `FILE` without installing it or writing results |

## pudl policy list

List loaded policies with their stored result counts

```text
pudl policy list [flags]
```

```text
List every loaded compliance policy: the type it applies to, the policy it
extends, its rule count, the type's review status (draft results are
provisional), when it was last evaluated, and its stored compliant,
noncompliant, unknown and stale result counts. A result is stale when it was
evaluated with an older version of the policy; pudl policy evaluate refreshes it.

--type T lists the policies that apply to type T.
```

Examples:

```bash
pudl policy list
  pudl policy list --type pudl/aws.#Bucket --json
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--type` | string |  | List only the policies that apply to type `T` |

## pudl policy show

Show a policy's rules, inheritance and failing resources

```text
pudl policy show POLICY [flags]
```

```text
Show one compliance policy: its inheritance chain, its rules (inherited ones
included) with severity, doc and the policy that declared each, how many
resources currently fail each rule, its stored result counts and staleness, and
the resources failing most (most severe first, then most violations).

Each failing resource names its owner, derived from its type's _pudl.owner
declaration; --owner lists only that owner's failing resources.

--limit caps the failing resources listed (0 lists all).
```

Examples:

```bash
pudl policy show pudl/aws.#BucketBestPractice
  pudl policy show pudl/aws.#BucketBestPractice --limit 0 --json
  pudl policy show pudl/aws.#BucketBestPractice --owner payments
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--limit` | int | `10` | Maximum failing resources to list (0 = all) |
| `--owner` | string |  | List only the failing resources this owner owns (_pudl.owner) |

## pudl prime

Output agent prompt describing how to use pudl

```text
pudl prime
```

```text
Print a structured prompt that teaches AI agents how to use pudl.

Include a line like this in your CLAUDE.md or similar agent config:

    Run 'pudl prime' to learn how to use pudl.

The agent will then know to execute the command and read the output
to understand pudl's capabilities and conventions.
```

## pudl query

Query derived facts using Datalog rules

```text
pudl query <relation> [--field=value ...] [flags]
```

```text
Evaluate Datalog rules over the fact store and catalog, then query results.

Rules come from the project and its explicitly vendored dependencies.
Project rules have highest priority. Use --global for personal workspace rules.

Ad-hoc rules can be loaded from a file with -f.

Positional constraints filter results (field=value pairs). JSON numeric values
are parsed without rounding; other unquoted values are strings. To match a
numeric-looking string, retain JSON quotes, e.g. 'id="123"'.

Temporal modes (determined by which flags are set):
  (none)           Evaluate over current facts
  --as-of-valid    Evaluate over facts true at a point in time
  --as-of-tx       Evaluate over facts known at a point in time
  (both)           Evaluate over what was believed at --as-of-tx about --as-of-valid

Use --list to see the relations (rule heads + EDB facts) you can query and the
arg keys each expects. Use --topo to read a relation's from/to edges as a
topological run order (dependencies first); it errors on a cycle.

Examples:
    pudl query --list
    pudl query depends_transitive
    pudl query depends_transitive from=api
    pudl query impacted_by changed=network
    pudl query --topo model_depends_on
    pudl query -f my-analysis.cue corroborated_obstacle
    pudl query observation --as-of-valid 2026-04-01T14:30:00Z
    pudl query depends_transitive --json
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--all-workspaces` | bool |  | Include global rules and all workspace data |
| `--as-of-tx` | string |  | Evaluate over facts known at this time (RFC3339 or Unix) |
| `--as-of-valid` | string |  | Evaluate over facts true at this time (RFC3339 or Unix) |
| `--list` | bool |  | List queryable relations (rule heads + EDB facts) and their arg keys |
| `--max-iterations` | int | `100` | Cap on fixpoint rounds per recursive cycle (the longest chain a recursive rule can follow) |
| `-f`, `--rule-file` | string |  | Load additional rules from a CUE file |
| `--timeout` | duration |  | Maximum query duration (0 disables deadline) |
| `--topo` | bool |  | Read the relation's from/to edges as a topological run order (errors on a cycle) |

In a project, rules come from `.pudl/schema/pudl/rules/` and the rules of
vendored dependencies; in global mode, from `~/.pudl/schema/pudl/rules/`. A
query fails when the queried relation depends on a rule that cannot be loaded;
`pudl doctor` lists such rules. See [Datalog](datalog.md) for rules,
built-in relations and time travel.

Every positional constraint must be `field=value` with a nonblank field;
repeated fields are errors. Empty values and values containing `=` are valid.
`--list` takes no positional arguments and cannot be combined with `--topo`.
`--max-iterations` must be nonnegative; zero uses the default.
`--timeout` bounds evaluation and waiting for writers; a cancelled query
returns an error, never a partial answer. If stdout fails mid-write, a
consumer may receive a prefix, so automation must check the exit status.

## pudl report

Read the latest or named check report

```text
pudl report [ID] [flags]
```

```text
Read a stored report: the newest one, or the one ID names.

ID is a check ID, or the run ID of one model within a check. Reports recorded
by the retired "pudl run" and "pudl run set" commands read the same way;
fields those reports carry that current reports do not are shown as recorded
under "legacy fields".

With --since ID2 it compares instead: each check's failing matches in the
report against the same check in report ID2, model by model, as new,
persisting, resolved, or unknown when the report cannot establish their
absence.

Examples:
    pudl report
    pudl report check_... --json
    pudl report check_B --since check_A
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--since` | string |  | compare the report's check findings with an earlier report (check ID or run ID): new, persisting, resolved, unknown |

With no ID, `report` reads the newest stored report; with an ID, that report:
a check ID, or the run ID of one model within a check. `--json` prints the
report as stored. Reports keep their historical values and witnesses; reading
one adds whether its evidence snapshots are still available, without
recomputing findings (see
[evidence lifetime](evidence.md#reports-and-evidence-lifetime)).

`--since ID2` compares instead of printing: each check's findings are
classified against the same check in ID2, models paired by name, as `new`,
`persisting`, `resolved` or `unknown`. A check is skipped when ID2 lacks it,
reached no verdict for it, or evaluated it differently. `--json` writes
`report`, `since`, and per model each check's `changes` and `findings`. See
[changes over time](governance.md#track-changes-over-time).

Reports recorded by the retired `pudl run` and `pudl run set` read the same
way. Older run-set reports (versions 1 and 2) carry only member summaries;
read a member with `pudl report RUN_ID`. Fields current reports no longer
have are shown under "legacy fields".

```text
(fields with head and body). The file is validated before installation.

By default, rules are installed repo-scoped (.pudl/schema/pudl/rules/).
Use --global to install to ~/.pudl/schema/pudl/rules/.

Examples:
```

Manage CUE schemas for data validation


```text
Manage CUE schemas for import validation and resource identity.

Schemas come from the project and its explicit vendored dependencies, or the
personal workspace selected by --global. Use list/show for discovery and add/new
for authoring; pudl doctor --fix repairs schema names and inference drift.
Inspect physical paths with pudl config --paths --json. Git, your editor, and cue
manage the files directly; see docs/retired-commands.md for replacements.
```

Subcommands:

- [pudl schema add](#pudl-schema-add) — Add a new schema to the repository
- [pudl schema list](#pudl-schema-list) — List schema definitions and resource metadata

- [pudl schema show](#pudl-schema-show) — Display the contents of a schema

## pudl schema add

Add a new schema to the repository

```text
pudl schema add <package>.<name> <cue-file>
```

```text
Add a CUE schema file to the workspace schema directory.

The schema name has the form 'package.name':
- package: the schema package directory (aws, gcp, custom, ...)
- name: the file name within the package (written as <name>.cue)

The file must compile as CUE; syntax, build and validation errors stop the
add. Warnings are printed but do not stop it. Declare identity, sensitive
fields, facts, ownership and review status in the definition's _pudl block;
see docs/schema-authoring.md.

The file is copied into the package directory. It is not committed to git.

Examples:
    pudl schema add aws.rds-instance rds-schema.cue
    pudl schema add k8s.deployment my-deployment.cue
    pudl schema add custom.api-response api.cue
```

## pudl schema list

List schema definitions and resource metadata

```text
pudl schema list [flags]
```

```text
List schemas using full package.#Definition names accepted by 'pudl schema show'.
The listing includes resource types. Use --verbose for source paths, identity fields
and collection metadata, or --json for the complete representation.
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--package` | string |  | Filter by package name |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | bool |  | Show paths and schema metadata |

Full `package.#Definition` names can be passed directly to `schema show`.
Workspace definitions shadow global definitions. JSON includes source paths,
built-in status, and available `_pudl` metadata; verbose text includes identity
fields and list type information.

## pudl schema new

Generate a new schema from imported data

```text
pudl schema new [flags]
```

```text
Generate a new CUE schema by analyzing data from a previously imported entry.

This command creates a new schema file based on the structure of imported data,
inferring field types, identifying likely identity fields, and generating
appropriate CUE type definitions.

The --from flag specifies the proquint ID of the imported data to analyze.
The --path flag specifies where to create the schema (package path and definition name).

If the path contains a # character, everything after it is used as the definition name.
Otherwise, the last path component is capitalized and used as the definition name.

When --from points to a collection entry:
- Without --collection: analyzes individual items to create an item schema
- With --collection: creates a schema for the collection structure itself

The --infer flag allows specifying type hints for specific fields, such as
marking a field as an enum type.

An item schema gets a _pudl graph block, so the type draws in pudl ui: name,
account and region fields guessed from the data, display {code, label,
class} guessed from the definition name, and the view roles as commented
examples. Check it with 'pudl graph vocab'.

Examples:
    pudl schema new --from hugib-dubuf --path aws/ec2:#Instance
    pudl schema new --from govim-nupab --path aws/ec2:#Instance  # from collection
    pudl schema new --from govim-nupab --path aws/ec2:#InstanceCollection --collection
    pudl schema new --from hugib-dubuf --path aws/ec2:#Instance --infer State=enum
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--collection` | bool |  | Create a collection schema instead of item schema |
| `--force` | bool |  | Overwrite existing schema files |
| `--from` | string |  | Proquint ID of the imported data to generate schema from (required) |
| `--infer` | stringArray |  | Field inference hints (e.g., State=enum) |
| `--path` | string |  | Schema path in format 'package/path:#Definition' (required) |

```text
Examples:
```


```text
Show detailed information about a specific data entry including its content,
metadata, and schema information.

A compliance section lists each policy applicable to the entry's type with the
resource's stored status (provisional when the type is a draft), its highest
violation severity, and its violations (rule, severity, path, kind, declaring

The ID parameter should be the unique identifier of the data entry as shown

Display Options:

    pudl show 20250825_222510_test-data --metadata --raw # Show everything
```

| `--history` | bool |  | Show this resource's stored versions and snapshot observations |
| `--metadata` | bool |  | Show metadata file content |
| `--raw` | bool |  | Show raw data content |

## pudl snapshot

Inspect and retain observation snapshots

```text
pudl snapshot
```

```text
Observation snapshots are what a run saw.

Each populate or observe ingest records one snapshot: which model it was taken
for, by which run, in which workspace, from which source, and how many records it
holds. A snapshot ID is what "pudl check <model> --from-catalog --catalog-scope <id>"
replays against.

Snapshots accumulate — one per run, plus one raw file per record — so they need
pruning. Pruning is explicit and never happens as a side effect of a run.

Examples:
    pudl snapshot list --model k8sPolicy
    pudl snapshot current k8sPolicy
    pudl snapshot retain snap_kisut-hipol
    pudl snapshot prune --model k8sPolicy --keep 5 --older-than 720h --dry-run
```

Subcommands:

- [pudl snapshot current](#pudl-snapshot-current) — Show the newest observation snapshot for a model
- [pudl snapshot list](#pudl-snapshot-list) — List observation snapshots, newest first
- [pudl snapshot prune](#pudl-snapshot-prune) — Remove snapshots a retention policy no longer wants
- [pudl snapshot retain](#pudl-snapshot-retain) — Pin a snapshot against pruning (--release to unpin)
- [pudl snapshot show](#pudl-snapshot-show) — Show one snapshot's provenance and contents

Each observation is one snapshot with a scope and a completeness flag (see
[observation](observation-scope.md)). `snapshot show NEW --compare OLD`
compares two snapshots of one scope: a resource missing from NEW is `removed`
only when NEW is complete, and `not-observed` otherwise. A snapshot can be
pinned by reports (for 30 days), by `snapshot retain`, or by legacy
approvals; `prune` removes none of them, nor a model's latest successful
observation. See [evidence lifetime](evidence.md#reports-and-evidence-lifetime).

## pudl snapshot current

Show the newest observation snapshot for a model

```text
pudl snapshot current <model>
```

## pudl snapshot list

List observation snapshots, newest first

```text
pudl snapshot list [flags]
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--limit` | int | `20` | maximum rows (0 = no limit) |
| `--model` | string |  | only this model's snapshots |

## pudl snapshot prune

Remove snapshots a retention policy no longer wants

```text
pudl snapshot prune [flags]
```

```text
Remove old observation snapshots, their records and their raw files.

--keep and --older-than are an AND: a snapshot goes only if it is outside the
newest N for its model AND older than the cutoff. That means --keep 0 alone
removes nothing, which is deliberate — a prune that empties a model's history
because a flag defaulted to zero is the more expensive surprise.

Records are shared between snapshots by content, so a record is removed only
when no remaining snapshot cites it. Retained snapshots, and snapshots recorded
before the snapshot contract existed, are never removed.
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | report what would be removed, remove nothing |
| `--keep` | int | `10` | always keep this many newest per model |
| `--model` | string |  | only this model's snapshots |
| `--older-than` | duration |  | only remove snapshots older than this (e.g. 720h) |

## pudl snapshot retain

Pin a snapshot against pruning (--release to unpin)

```text
pudl snapshot retain <snapshot-id> [flags]
```

```text
Add a manual pin so no retention policy removes this snapshot.
--release removes only the manual pin; legacy approval and retained-report owners remain.
Reports preserve referenced snapshot evidence for 30 days after their last save.

Snapshots recorded before snapshot provenance existed cannot be pinned — they
carry no contract row — but they are never pruned either, for the same reason.
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--release` | bool |  | unpin instead of pinning |

## pudl snapshot show

Show one snapshot's provenance and contents

```text
pudl snapshot show <snapshot-id> [flags]
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--compare` | string |  | Compare this snapshot with an older snapshot; incomplete absence stays unproven |

## pudl status

Show the verified status of models and targets

```text
pudl status [target]
```

```text
Display the status recorded in the catalog — the per-target verdict
pudl check writes (a model's verdict is recorded on its instance row,
"//models/<name>").

Status values:
  unknown     — no verified status recorded yet (the retired "converging" value also reads as unknown)
  clean       — observed == desired, confirmed by a live observation
  drifted     — observed != desired, or a fail-severity check did not pass
  failed      — recorded by the retired convergence workflow; check the model again to replace it

Examples:
    pudl status
    pudl status //models/github-chazu
    pudl status --json
```

Status is recorded per model target by `pudl check`. `clean` means a live
observation matched `desired` and no fail-severity check failed; it is never
written by a `--from-catalog` replay. `drifted` means drift or a failing
fail-severity check. `unknown` means no verdict: the model has no `desired`
state, has not been observed, or its last check could not establish one (an
incomplete inventory, a check without evidence). `failed` and the value
`converging` appear only on rows written by retired commands; `converging`
reads as `unknown`, and the next check replaces both.

## pudl ui

Open the graph explorer on this workspace's catalog

```text
pudl ui [flags]
```

```text
Serve the web graph explorer, embedded in the pudl binary, and open it in
a browser. The explorer reads the workspace catalog live: every load or
Reload shows the current resources and relationships (the same graph as
'pudl graph export').

The server is read-only and listens on the loopback interface. It answers
only requests addressed to that host, so other web pages cannot read the
inventory. Serving on another interface exposes the inventory to anyone who
can reach it, so it needs --allow-remote.

The UI refreshes itself when the catalog, the rules or the schemas change
(for example when a 'pudl check' finishes in another terminal), keeping the
current view.

Examples:
    pudl ui
    pudl ui --addr 127.0.0.1:9000 --no-open
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--addr` | string | `127.0.0.1:7468` | Address to listen on (port 0 picks a free port) |
| `--allow-remote` | bool |  | Allow a non-loopback --addr (exposes the inventory) |
| `--no-open` | bool |  | Do not open a browser |

## Advanced commands

These commands are supported but left out of everyday help: `--help`
listings and shell completion omit them, and `pudl help --json` marks them
`"advanced": true`. Run them by their full path.

- [pudl facts add](#pudl-facts-add) — Add a fact to the bitemporal store (the canonical write)
- [pudl facts invalidate](#pudl-facts-invalidate) — Invalidate a fact (mark as no longer true)
- [pudl facts retract](#pudl-facts-retract) — Retract a fact (mark as no longer asserted)

## pudl facts add

Add a fact to the bitemporal store (the canonical write)

```text
pudl facts add [flags]
```

```text
Add a fact under any relation using a JSON object. Facts are general-purpose.
Use --schema to validate the args against an authored CUE schema before storing them.

Examples:
    pudl facts add --relation depends --args '{"from":"api","to":"database"}'
    pudl facts add --relation config --args '{"key":"timeout","value":30}' --source operator
```

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--args` | string |  | Fact body as a JSON object (required) |
| `--relation` | string |  | Relation to write (required) |
| `--schema` | string |  | Validate args against a named on-disk CUE schema (e.g. user/config.#Setting) |
| `--source` | string |  | Source of the fact (agent name or username; defaults to the current OS user) |

## pudl facts invalidate

Invalidate a fact (mark as no longer true)

```text
pudl facts invalidate <id>
```

```text
Record that a fact stopped being true now.

Use this when reality changed — the fact was correct when recorded but
is no longer true. The fact remains visible in historical queries
(--as-of-valid) but disappears from current queries.

History is not rewritten: the recorded version is closed and a new version
with a valid end time supersedes it, so --as-of-tx queries for earlier
moments still show what was believed then. The new version's ID is printed.

Examples:
    pudl facts invalidate c0b4392d347aca8e...
```

## pudl facts retract

Retract a fact (mark as no longer asserted)

```text
pudl facts retract <id>
```

```text
Mark a fact as retracted by setting its transaction end time.

Use this when a fact was recorded in error — the assertion was wrong.
The fact remains in the store for audit purposes but disappears from
current queries.

Examples:
    pudl facts retract c0b4392d347aca8e...
```
